FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Solid Mineral Fuels and Solid Biofuels Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal 
and Related Products Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1966 and covered graphical symbols prevalent at that time. 


The first revision of this standard was undertaken in 1984, which was based on Document 27/N 1334 ‘Coal 
preparation plant — Graphical symbols’ issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). 


In coal preparation industry, flow diagram are widely used as a first drawing to show the basic items of major 
equipment and their relationship to one another in the entire process. Graphical symbols for the equipment used 
in a process, when connected by the flow lines, describe the sequence of operations in it. 


Keeping in view the continuous process of establishment of a large number of coal preparation plants in the 
country, it was felt that formulation of standard on graphical symbols will simplify the exchange of information 
among those concerned with the design, construction and operation of coal preparation installations. 


In this revision, considerable assistance has been taken from ISO 561: 1989 ‘Coal preparation plant — Graphical 
symbols’. Most of the symbol given in ISO 561 : 1989 have been incorporated in this standard. The main points 
of difference relate to feeders, breakers, crushers and some types of screens. Additional symbols for sieve-bend or 
arc screen, fixed screen or grizzley, demagnetizer, liquid reagent feeder and heavy medium cyclone washer, etc, 
have been added. 


For symbols used in the basic process flow diagrams for representing the major items of equipment used by the 
petroleum and chemical industries, those recommended in IS 3232 : 1999 ‘Recommendations on graphical symbols 
for process flow diagrams, piping and instrumentation diagrams (first revision)’ shall be used. 


Indian Standard 


GRAPHICAL SYMBOLS FOR 
COAL PREPARATION PLANT 


(Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes basic symbols for use in the 
process flow diagrams and others relating to coal 
preparation plants. 


2 PRINCIPLES 


2.1 The symbols incorporated in this standard have been 
selected in accordance with the following principles: 


a) The items of the plant listed shall be widely 
used for coal preparation and required to be 
identified on flow sheets. 

b) The symbols shall be easy to draw and 
distinguishable readily from one another. 

c) The symbols shall preferably give some 
indications of the principle of the separation 
involved, but shall not represent the 
appearance of any particular type of machine. 


3 CONVENTIONS FOR THE DRAWING OF 
SYMBOLS 


3.1 The following conventions shall be adopted for 
drawing the standard symbols: 


a) The plant symbols shall be shown by heavy 
lines and the product flow by light lines. 


b) In general the flow lines shall enter the 
symbols from above or from the left and shall 
leave the symbol downwards or to the right. 


c) Where more than one product enters or leave 
an item of plant, the numbers of entry, and 
exit arrows shall be varied accordingly. 


d) Graphical symbols have been grouped under 
4 distinct process headings as follows: 


1) Receipt and pre-treatment of feed coal, 
2) Cleaning, 
3) Subsequent treatment of products, and 


4) End product planning, storage and 
disposal. 


3.2 An alphabetical index of symbols is given in 
Annex A for information only. 


IS 3746 : 2018

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: PCD 07 (2771).
